matches.rationale: No finding identifies the Abstract's misreporting of a 3.5 trillion token dataset and swapping of 15B/15A2B models. Pred1 cites a different inconsistency (1 trillion tokens, 30B MoE, 3.4B dense), so the underlying issue is not the same.

Pred12 directly identifies the contradictory claim in Section 3.2.1 that key-layer gating (G3) yields superior performance, which conflicts with Table 1 showing G3 is worse than baseline. This captures the exact method-logic inconsistency of the ground truth.

No finding explicitly points to the exaggerated claim that gating enables stable training at much higher learning rates and eliminates loss spikes, nor that Table 2 and loss plots do not support this. Stability overstatements are not addressed.

Pred13 observes that the data in Table 1 does not support the claim that G2 is most effective, mirroring the ground-truth corruption where Table 1 data was altered to show smaller/inconsistent gains, thus contradicting performance claims.
No finding mentions the fabricated references [80], [81], [82] or the inflation of background support with non-existent citations in the Related Work section.
No finding detects the removal of ethical impacts/limitations discussion from the Appendix (A.5). The findings do not address omissions of broader-impact statements.

The ground-truth error is about the Abstract claiming gating 'completely eliminates attention sinks.' Pred6 does not match because it cites the Abstract saying 'partially alleviates' and focuses on the title vs. body inconsistency, not an unqualified elimination claim.
No finding captures the misalignment that the Abstract claims gating tolerates larger learning rates, while the Experiments section shows higher LRs cause divergence even with gating.

Pred9 highlights the contradictory statements about hyperparameter tuning for gating variants (no tuning performed vs. benefit from increased learning rate), matching the ground truth that selectively reports optimized hyperparameters only for baselines, biasing results against gating.
No finding mentions the fabricated or post-dated arXiv references ([6] and [20]) from 2025 that compromise the factual accuracy of the reference list.

No finding detects the overstatement in the Discussion that gating completely eliminates attention sinks and massive activations, whereas figures and tables show only partial reduction. Pred6 and pred15 address related but different issues.

No finding points to the omission of instability or divergence instances at larger learning rates for gating variants, which would have revealed cherry-picked positive results. Stability shortcomings are not addressed.

Pred4 addresses ambiguity about which hidden states serve as gate input, not the ground-truth corruption that the gating formula was altered from multiplicative to additive, causing a core definitional contradiction.
None of the findings identify the deliberate shift in gating score distributions in Figure 3 and Appendix A.6 to show less sparsity. Pred11 discusses Table 4, not the altered figures/appendix.

No finding detects the Conclusion's claim that gating 'eliminates attention sinks' while the Appendix retains residual attention sinks. Pred6 involves the Abstract, not the Conclusion vs. Appendix misalignment.

No finding explicitly notes that negative or neutral outcomes of head-shared gating variants are omitted from the paper. Pred15 discusses a specific contradiction but does not point to a systematic omission of contrary evidence.
